direction.premise: A compact crash-test yard where accumulated dents and mechanical failures remain on the driven car.
direction.composition: A large readable damaged vehicle in a garage inspection stage (side-aligned controls on desktop, vehicle above bottom controls on phones), then an independent fixed-angle or chasing 3D physical crash course.
direction.shapeLanguage: Each car class has a purpose-built continuous crushable shell, independent damageable roof, furnished glazing, detailed alloy-and-rubber wheels; collision obstacles use industrial form and hazard geometry.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Automotive enamel with accumulating scuffed vertex color, dark rubber, machined aluminum, blue-tinted glazing, chipped concrete and yellow industrial safety signage.
direction.paletteLogic: Muted daylight concrete is the field; vivid automotive paint makes local deformation visible. Yellow collision warnings contrast with dark galvanized crash structures.
direction.typography: Existing compact instrument labels remain around the perimeter. New camera switches have explicit Russian labels in the garage and pause sheet.
direction.signature: Switch from an indexed garage test plinth to a physics obstacle field. Wheel motion, force measurements, dents, and a persistent reverse gear all derive from real simulated objects.
direction.distinction: FOG exposes geographical strategy and MEAT.EXE uses first-person navigation; this camera frames a third-person deforming vehicle in a fixed world direction.

architecture.primaryVerb: Hold the gas pedal while steering the car into crash-test obstacles; inspect lasting body deformation and handling changes.
architecture.physicalFeedback: The vehicle accelerates with mass and steering response; contacts deform its shell and kick the camera, then debris and damaged mechanical parts remain.
architecture.spatialRationale: A stable world azimuth makes turns readable on a phone while the car-following translation preserves useful surrounding road space and two-handed driving.

comparisons.spatialDifference: fog-of-conquest uses full-bleed-world with diegetic-tools; CRUMPLE centers a vehicle in a freely traversable three-dimensional industrial yard.
comparisons.interactionDifference: fog-of-conquest uses scene-zoom and immediate; here the driver continuously modulates steering and gas while contacts permanently change the same vehicle.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Perekos stages compact 2D duels with pixel sprites; CRUMPLE features a full-screen freely driven 3D industrial collision range and dimensional cars.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Perekos emphasizes precision projectile combat; CRUMPLE responds to continuous wheel input and accumulates contact-based physical deformation.

comparisons.spatialDifference: PetriForge presents agent lab boards and trajectory analysis; CRUMPLE centers a deformable third-person vehicle within a rigid-body test yard.
comparisons.interactionDifference: PetriForge controls training and agent experiments; CRUMPLE is an immediately controllable car with post-impact drivability changes.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Katana Echo is a timber sword-fighting dojo dominated by a 2D-like melee duel lane; CRUMPLE is a physically traversable Babylon test yard, with a separate inspection plinth and a large 3D car that can rotate.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Katana Echo is direct sword slashes, guarded movement and replayed shadows; CRUMPLE is analog throttle/steering, Rapier suspension forces and contact-dependent long-lived structural damage.

production.renderer: Babylon WebGL renders the existing segmented car meshes while Rapier solves rigid-body contacts and the damage system updates shell vertices.
production.focalAsset: Dense, car-specific deformable shell rings maintain cumulative deformation; a separately constructed non-colliding detail kit adds wheel arches, five-spoke alloys, framing, exterior trim and unique body variants.

motion.character: Heavy translation and vehicle rotation carry the sense of mass; the fixed camera follows position with exponential settling.
motion.action: Drive into a barrier, then turn with the same camera azimuth to examine the accumulated damage.
motion.anticipation: The driver selects a car and a clearly labelled camera mode before leaving the garage.
motion.response: Gas and steering modify the next physics step; the camera target follows world position while vehicle heading does not rotate its view.
motion.followThrough: Camera translation settles smoothly, debris falls and damaged components keep changing driving behavior until repair.
motion.interruption: The pause switch snaps between fixed and chase framing immediately and persists the choice; rapid switching creates no queued transition.
motion.reducedMotion: No decorative camera orbit is introduced. Fixed framing removes heading-driven rotation while collision feedback continues to indicate a real impact.

evidence.expectedChange: The garage closes and the car is framed from a fixed world direction, with gas, steering and damage telemetry available.
